page: Vultr voc-g-4c-16gb-80s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured for general-purpose computing workloads. The server features 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz, supporting two threads per core. Memory capacity is 16 GB, providing a standard 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Local storage is provided via an integrated 80 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without bundled GPU acceleration.

Architecturally, the AMD x86_64 processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside vector extensions including AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. In benchmarking, the instance shows top-tier single-core CPU throughput in stress-ng and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 32.1 GB/sec. Large-block memory write throughput reaches a strong 113.87 GB/sec. Multi-core performance across stress-ng, Geekbench 6, and PassMark tests falls within the median range.

Resource constraints emerge in multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and large model inference, where lower core density and memory footprint limit throughput. Static web serving throughput and 7B parameter LLM inference demonstrate lower-tier relative results. Consequently, the instance offers balanced resource efficiency for medium-scale application tiers, backend services, CI/CD pipelines, lightweight caching with Redis, and general enterprise workloads that benefit from dedicated core isolation rather than dense thread counts.
description: Vultr voc-g-4c-16gb-80s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built for general-purpose workloads. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz across 2 physical cores, coupled with 16 GB of RAM and 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 32 MB of L3 cache along with AVX-512, VNNI, and hardware encryption instruction sets. In benchmark assessments, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core compute performance and strong memory write throughput, while overall multi-core and memory read metrics settle into mid-tier ranges. The configuration exhibits tradeoffs in intensive database operations and large-scale language model execution due to its four-thread envelope. It provides consistent resource allocation without GPU acceleration, making it an efficient choice for application hosting, build environments, and containerized microservices.
